profile.campus: Henderson, Clark County, Nevada (West Warm Springs Road, 64-acre site, two parcels east of Boulder Highway)
profile.address: 540 West Warm Springs Road, Henderson, Clark County, Nevada, 89011
profile.reading:
This building, addressed 540 West Warm Springs Road, is one of two Google has built on a 64-acre Henderson, Nevada site spanning two parcels east of Boulder Highway. Google subsidiary Design LLC filed the original application through Nevada's Governor's Office of Economic Development, and Clark County approved it in November 2018 as a $600 million project expected to create at least 50 permanent positions averaging around $31 an hour, plus more than 3,000 temporary construction jobs. Henderson Mayor Debra March and Google formally announced the partnership in July 2019, and the state granted Google roughly $25 million in tax abatements over 20 years while the company was still projected to pay more than $85 million in state and local taxes over that period. Google returned to expand the project less than two years later: in September 2020 the company announced an additional $600 million investment, doubling its cumulative Henderson commitment to $1.2 billion and adding at least 50 more full-time positions at an average annual salary of about $65,000. The facility supports Google Cloud alongside core consumer services including Search, YouTube, and Gmail for the western United States. Google's Nevada data center location page did not resolve to a working page when checked this session, so this reading relies on Las Vegas Sun and Las Vegas Review-Journal reporting rather than Google's own site; Google has not disclosed which of the two Warm Springs Road buildings, 540 or 560, serves which function, nor either building's individual square footage or MW capacity.

NV Energy, the regulated utility serving Henderson, has cited large-load data center customers including Google among the drivers behind its own long-range resource planning filings with the Nevada Public Utilities Commission, and Nevada's state and local incentive packages for data centers, including the abatements Google received, have periodically drawn scrutiny from state lawmakers weighing how much tax revenue such deals forgo against the jobs and investment they attract.

reading.body:
Google operates a confirmed data center in Henderson, Nevada at 540 West Warm Springs Road. The facility's power capacity is not published. Google's disclosure policy limits public information on individual facilities to aggregate state-level investment figures, so the specific megawatt capacity, square footage, and detailed specifications of this campus are not available from the operator.

Nevada has 26 mapped data center facilities, of which only two publish power capacity figures. This Henderson site ranks third among Nevada facilities by published megawatt capacity, though that ranking reflects the scarcity of published data rather than a complete ranking of all sites in the state. The two facilities with published figures account for 10.37 MW total in Nevada, but this sum excludes the vast majority of mapped capacity whose operators do not disclose figures.

Whether this campus matters to AI scaling cannot be assessed from published specifications. The absence of disclosed power capacity means the site cannot be placed within national or global data center rankings. To evaluate its significance to AI compute availability and grid strain, direct disclosure from Google or regulatory filings with capacity figures would be required.
